title: Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs has launched an upgraded version of the National Youth Parliament Scheme web portal, known as NYPS 2.0
body_text:
The Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs has launched an upgraded version of the National Youth Parliament Scheme (NYPS) web portal, known as NYPS 2.0 on 11 th September 2024. Unlike the previous version, which was limited to students of recognized institutions only, NYPS 2.0 is open to all the educational institutions, groups and citizens across the country. Since its launch the details of institutional, group and individual registrations recorded and sittings conducted under each mode on the portal are as follows:
Period Institution Participation Group Participation Individual Participation Total number of participating Citizens/ Students (A+B+C) No. of Registrations No. of Events Organized (No. of YPSs*) No. of Participating Students (A) No. of Registrations No. of Events Organized (No. of YPSs) No. of participating Citizens/ Students (B) No. of participating Citizens/ Students (C) Since Launch on 11-09-2024 to 21-07-2026 4939 1611 54518 732 26 982 48291 103791
The details of 42 on boarded Consultative Committees for various Ministries are available on the Consultative Committee Management System (CCMS) portal of the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs i.e. https://oams.nic.in/ccms/index.aspx , which is an accessible document.
To strengthen the outreach of the NYPS web portal, the Ministry has written to all State Governments, Union Territory Administrations; Legislatures of States/UTs; various educational boards (CBSE, CISCE), and also a publicity video tutorial is broadcast from time to time on Sansad TV. The CCMS portal has been continuously upgraded digitally from time to time as per requirement of stakeholders.
This information was given by the Minister of State of Parliamentary Affairs, Dr. L. Murugan in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha today.
***
ISA

enrichment.summary: The Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs informed the Rajya Sabha that its upgraded National Youth Parliament Scheme (NYPS 2.0) web portal, launched on 11 September 2024, has expanded participation beyond recognized institutions to include groups and individual citizens. Between launch and 21 July 2026, the portal recorded 4,939 institutional registrations (1,611 events, 54,518 student participants) and 732 group registrations (26 events, 982 participants), along with 48,291 individual participants, totaling 103,791 participants. The Ministry also maintains a Consultative Committee Management System (CCMS) portal listing 42 onboarded Consultative Committees and has undertaken outreach via states/UTs, education boards, and Sansad TV.
enrichment.context:
The National Youth Parliament Scheme (NYPS) is a Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs initiative aimed at inculcating parliamentary culture, democratic values, and awareness of legislative procedures among youth by simulating parliamentary debates and proceedings. Traditionally confined to recognized educational institutions, the scheme's digitization and broadening to individuals and groups under NYPS 2.0 reflects a wider push toward using digital platforms (Digital India ethos) to deepen civic and political literacy, especially among youth who form a significant demographic dividend in India's polity.

Consultative Committees, referenced in the release via the CCMS portal, are informal parliamentary mechanisms where MPs from both Houses interact with ministries to discuss policies without binding recommendatory power, distinct from formal Departmentally Related Standing Committees. Their digitization aims to enhance transparency and accessibility of these interactions between the legislature and executive, relevant to the broader theme of parliamentary oversight mechanisms in India's governance structure.

prelims_questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the National Youth Parliament Scheme (NYPS) 2.0:
1. It is administered by the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs.
2. Under NYPS 2.0, participation is restricted only to students of recognized educational institutions.
3. It allows registration through institutional, group, and individual modes.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
prelims_questions.explanation: NYPS is run by the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs (statement 1 correct). Unlike the earlier version, NYPS 2.0 removed the restriction to recognized institutions and opened participation to groups and individual citizens as well (statement 2 incorrect, statement 3 correct).

prelims_questions.question: The Consultative Committees for various Union Ministries, whose details are managed via the CCMS portal, are best described as:
options: Statutory bodies created under an Act of Parliament with binding powers over ministries
Informal parliamentary mechanisms enabling MPs to discuss policy matters with ministries without binding recommendatory authority
Judicial bodies that review the constitutionality of ministry actions
Executive committees composed solely of bureaucrats without any MP membership
prelims_questions.explanation: Consultative Committees attached to various ministries are informal, non-statutory forums where Members of Parliament interact with ministers/officials to discuss policy issues; their recommendations are not binding on the government.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the significance of youth parliament schemes in strengthening democratic values and parliamentary culture among India's young population. In this context, evaluate the transition from NYPS to NYPS 2.0.

Examine the role of Consultative Committees attached to Union Ministries in India's parliamentary system. How does digitization of such mechanisms, as seen in the CCMS portal, contribute to legislative-executive engagement and transparency?
